title: Government's Responses to the "2026 Review of Salaries for Political Appointment Holders and Members of Parliament"
what_it_is: Government's Responses to the "2026 Review of Salaries for Political Appointment Holders and Members of Parliament"

sections.label: Committee reviews framework recommendations
sections.summary: The Committee reviewed the framework and made its recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Committee has reviewed the framework and made its recommendations.

sections.label: Framework affirmed with refinements
sections.summary: The Committee affirmed the framework remains sound, updated its parameters, recommended refinements, and said the proposed salary levels would not be moved to immediately.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Committee has affirmed that the framework remains sound, while updating its parameters and recommending some refinements.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we do not intend to move immediately to the proposed salary levels in one step.

sections.label: Political office holder salary norms unchanged
sections.summary: Salary norms for political office holders have remained unchanged for 15 years, with the gap most obvious against the private sector, and some senior Permanent Secretaries earn more than Ministers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a result, the salary norms for political office holders have remained unchanged for 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The gap is most obvious when compared with the private sector.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But even in the Public Service, some senior Permanent Secretaries earn more than Ministers.

sections.label: Acting now instead of neglect
sections.summary: The speaker decided that restraint cannot become neglect and that they must act now.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Restraint cannot become neglect – and that is why I have decided we must act now.

sections.label: Parenthood package and fiscal space
sections.summary: Civil servants can review schemes and propose improvements, but Minister Indranee and other political office holders in the workgroup shaped the overall parenthood package, and earlier difficult decisions including raising the GST give fiscal space for stronger family support.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Civil servants can review each scheme and propose improvements, but it was Minister Indranee and the other political office holders in the workgroup who looked at the parenthood journey as a whole and helped shape the overall package, deciding where support would make the greatest difference, how the cost would be shared between parents, employers and the Government, and how the different measures should fit together.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Successive governments have been careful about how we spend and disciplined about husbanding our resources.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That meant making difficult decisions including raising the Goods and Services Tax (GST) when we knew our spending needs would rise.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And because we acted earlier, we now have the fiscal space to provide stronger support for families in a sustainable way.

sections.label: Housing supply sustained by MND Ministers
sections.summary: Successive MND Ministers including Minister Desmond Lee and now Minister Chee Hong Tat kept up housing supply, and after COVID-19 caused a major shortfall they ramped construction back up, leaving a stronger position for further housing moves.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On other occasions, it was because of difficult site constraints.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But successive Ministry of National Development (MND) Ministers, including Minister Desmond Lee and now Minister Chee Hong Tat, have kept up the supply because Singaporeans will continue to need homes.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: When COVID-19 caused a major shortfall, they worked hard to ramp construction back up and recover lost ground.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that sustained effort is why we are now in a stronger position to make further moves on housing.

sections.label: Political service sacrifices tension
sections.summary: His experience shows political systems must balance politics as service against sacrifices that deter capable people.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: His experience illustrates the basic tension every political system has to manage: politics must remain a calling to serve our fellow citizens, but if the personal and financial sacrifices become too large, many capable people will simply choose to do something else.

sections.label: Clean wage political remuneration
sections.summary: Deliberate choices produced open political remuneration: competitive salaries with substantial discount, no hidden components or perks, called a clean wage.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We achieved it through deliberate choices made over many decades about how our political system should be designed and how it should work.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And one of those choices was to deal with political remuneration openly.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We recognised that highly able people have alternatives outside politics, so we pay political office holders' salaries that are competitive, but with a substantial discount to reflect political service.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There are no hidden salary components or perks outside the published framework.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is what we mean by a clean wage.

sections.label: Substantial MP allowance
sections.summary: The MP allowance is substantial, not a token, because MPs carry substantial responsibilities in Parliament and constituencies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We chose not to treat the MP allowance as a token allowance.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is a substantial allowance because MPs carry substantial responsibilities in Parliament and in their constituencies.

sections.label: 1970 Ministerial salaries raised
sections.summary: When Ministerial salaries were first raised in 1970, Mr Lee Kuan Yew said one reason was to appoint Mr Hon Sui Sen as Finance Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, when Ministerial salaries were first raised in 1970, Mr Lee Kuan Yew explained in Parliament that one reason was to enable him to appoint Mr Hon Sui Sen, who was then head of the Development Bank of Singapore, as Finance Minister.

sections.label: Renewal efforts and salary cuts
sections.summary: This was despite Senior Minister Lee's sustained renewal efforts, and the 2012 salary reduction and 15 years without benchmark adjustments made it harder.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This was despite Senior Minister Lee's sustained efforts to renew the team.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And the reduction in political salaries in 2012, followed by 15 years without adjustments to the benchmark did not make the task any easier.

sections.label: Younger officers brought in
sections.summary: None were prepared to move, but he brought in younger officers with strong potential and longer runways, like Mr Jeffrey Siow, Mr David Neo and Ms Jasmine Lau.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the end, none was prepared to make the move, but I was able to bring in younger officers with strong potential and a longer runway ahead of them, like Mr Jeffrey Siow, Mr David Neo and Ms Jasmine Lau.

sections.label: Ministers reaching 70
sections.summary: By the next term of Government, all three will be 70 and above, so planning should not assume they will continue helming these Ministries.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By the next term of Government, all three will be 70 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We should not plan on the basis that they will continue helming these Ministries then.

sections.label: Succession in four ministries
sections.summary: The succession challenge is very real in the Ministry of Finance, Trade and Industry, Home Affairs and Foreign Affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But ideally, I should have someone take over the Finance portfolio.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, when I look at the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the succession challenge is very real.

sections.label: Political salary and MP allowance changes
sections.summary: The Committee recommended updating the MR4 benchmark to $1.8 million and changing other salaries and MP allowances from 15 October 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Based on the latest data, the Committee has recommended updating the MR4 benchmark from $1.1 million to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It has also recommended changes to the other political office holder salaries and to MP allowances.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The revised framework will take effect from 15 October 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The monthly allowances for MPs will increase from $13,750 to $18,500 from that date.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister's salary is set at twice the MR4 benchmark.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I have decided that, for the next five years – assuming I remain Prime Minister – I will donate the full increase in my salary arising from this adjustment.

sections.label: One-off 9% adjustment
sections.summary: A one-off adjustment of up to 9% for political office holders will be made now.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Instead, we will make a one-off adjustment now of up to 9% for political office holders.

sections.label: MR4 Minister salary illustration
sections.summary: A full 9% adjustment would bring an MR4 Minister's $1.1 million salary to about $1.2 million, with no further special adjustments.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To illustrate, for an MR4 Minister earning the current reference salary of $1.1 million, the full 9% adjustment would bring the salary to about $1.2 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Thereafter, after this one-off adjustment, there will be no further special adjustments to close the gap to $1.8 million.

sections.label: Ministerial grades and salary ranges
sections.summary: The Committee recommended combining MR2 and MR3 grades into three Ministerial grades and widening each salary range to plus or minus 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Committee has recommended some fine-tuning to the current structure.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They have recommended that the MR2 and MR3 grades be combined.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, there will be three Ministerial grades instead of four.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They have also recommended that the salary range for each grade be widened to plus or minus 25%.

sections.label: Ministers' salaries at lower range
sections.summary: By the end of this term, most Ministers remaining at MR4 are expected to be at the lower end of the new salary range, about $1.35 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On that basis, by the end of this term of Government, I expect most Ministers who remain at MR4 to be at the lower-end of the new salary range – and that is about $1.35 million.

sections.label: Revised structure for differentiated pay
sections.summary: The revised structure gives the Prime Minister more room to differentiate pay by performance and attract experienced outsiders, while expecting meaningful sacrifice.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And this is the purpose of the revised structure.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It gives the Prime Minister more room to differentiate pay according to performance and importantly, to bring in people with substantial experience from outside Government, especially those already earning significantly more in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We still expect them to make a meaningful sacrifice to enter political service.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we should not make that gap larger than it needs to be.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Overall, I believe this will give me and future Prime Ministers a better chance of persuading capable Singaporeans to step forward and of building the strongest possible team for Singapore.

sections.label: Motion and updated salary framework
sections.summary: Minister Chan will move a Motion for both Ministerial Statements, with clarifications addressed during debate, and the salary framework must stay updated.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Minister Chan will give notice to move a Motion for both Ministerial Statements to be considered by Parliament after our Statements.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we will subsequently address Members' clarifications during the debate on the Motion.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that the salary framework stays updated so that capable and committed people from different backgrounds and at different stages of life, can step forward to serve, not just the financially independent ones or those who have made exceptional lifestyle choices.

sections.label: CEOs' earnings cited
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said some CEOs of major Singapore companies earn $6 million or $7 million a year, sometimes more.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister has said, some CEOs of major Singapore companies earn $6 million or $7 million a year, sometimes more.

sections.label: Frozen political salary structure
sections.summary: The current framework was established in 2012, political reference salaries have not been updated, a 2023 review was held back, and the structure has been frozen for 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The current framework was established in 2012, when the Government accepted the recommendations of the Committee led by Mr Gerard Ee.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Since then, the political reference salaries have not been updated.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We further held back a review in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And hence, the result is that the structure of political salaries has been frozen for the past 15 years.

sections.label: Independent Committee convened
sections.summary: As part of the review process, the Prime Minister convened an independent Committee in December last year.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As part of the review process, the Prime Minister convened an independent Committee in December last year.

sections.label: Core principles remain sound
sections.summary: The Government agrees with the Committee that the framework's three core principles remain sound and necessary for a strong, sustained political core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government agrees with the Committee's assessment that the three core principles of the framework remain sound and necessary so that we can build a strong, sustained political core.

sections.label: Discount off market benchmark
sections.summary: The discount is currently 40% off the market benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, the discount is 40% off the market benchmark.

sections.label: MR4 salary updated to $1.8m
sections.summary: The Government accepts the Committee's recommendation to update the MR4 reference annual salary to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: After reviewing the report, the Government has decided to accept the Committee's recommendation to update the MR4 reference annual salary to $1.8 million.

sections.label: Adjustment averages 3.6% yearly
sections.summary: Averaged over time, the adjustment works out to about 3.6% per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Averaging over time, the adjustment works out to be about 3.6% per year.

sections.label: One-off adjustment up to 9%
sections.summary: A one-off adjustment of up to 9% will be made depending on individual circumstances, including performance and last salary adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Instead, we will make a one-off adjustment of up to 9% for them, depending on individual circumstances, including performance and when his or her salary was last adjusted.

sections.label: Merging grades and setting pegs
sections.summary: MR2 and MR3 merge at 1.3 times MR4, and Mayors, Senior Parliamentary Secretaries and Parliamentary Secretaries are pegged at 0.45 times MR4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Specifically, we will combine the MR2 and MR3 Ministerial grades into a single grade, pegged at 1.3 times of MR4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is the midpoint between today's 1.2 and 1.4 times of the MR4 reference benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will also merge and set the peg for Mayors, Senior Parliamentary Secretaries and Parliamentary Secretaries at 0.45 times of MR4.

sections.label: Political appointment holders' salary components
sections.summary: Pay for political appointment holders has fixed and variable components split about 65:35.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The salary paid to political appointment holders comprises both fixed and variable pay components, with a split of about 65:35.

sections.label: Unemployment rate target level
sections.summary: The unemployment rate target will be tightened from 4% to 3% to below 3.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For unemployment rate, the target level will be tightened from the current 4% to below 4.5%, to 3% to below 3.5%.

sections.label: Real GDP growth target band
sections.summary: The real GDP growth target band will be updated from 3% to 5%, to 2% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For real gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate, the target band will be updated from 3% to 5%, to 2% to 4%.

sections.label: Amendments for President and Speaker
sections.summary: In October, the Government will move amendments and Motions for adjustments for the President, Speaker and Deputy Speakers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In October, the Government will move the necessary amendments and Motions to give effect to the adjustments for the President, Speaker and Deputy Speakers.

sections.label: MP allowances updated for inflation
sections.summary: The Government accepts the Committee's recommendation to update MP allowances from $13,750 to $18,500 monthly for inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In the meantime, the Government will accept the Committee's recommendation to update MP allowances from $13,750, to $18,500 monthly, to account for inflation.

sections.label: NCMP allowances and National Bonus
sections.summary: The Government accepts raising NCMP allowances from 15% to 30% of an MP's annual allowance, with revised allowances from 15 October and National Bonus from 1 January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government also accepts the Committee's recommendation to increase the allowance of Non-Constituency Members of Parliament (NCMPs), from 15% of an MP's annual allowance, to 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The revised allowances for all MPs will also be implemented with effect from 15 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The revised National Bonus framework will be implemented from 1 January 2027, as the data for the indicators are reported on a calendar year basis.

sections.label: Motion to consider Ministerial Statements
sections.summary: A Motion under Standing Order No 44 is given notice for Ministerial Statements on salaries to be considered on 10 September 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Members will no doubt have views on the Government's response and it is important that we hear them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why I will move a Motion for this House to consider the Statements made by the Prime Minister and myself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To give Members some time to consider both Ministerial Statements made today, I give notice to move a Motion under Standing Order No 44 for the Ministerial Statements, titled "Government's Response to the '2026 Committee Report on Review of Salaries for Political Appointment Holders and Members of Parliament'", to be considered by Parliament on Thursday, 10 September 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services has given notice that he will move a Motion under Standing Order No 44 for both Ministerial Statements to be considered by Parliament on 10 September 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Members will then have the opportunity to seek clarification and to debate on both Ministerial Statements at that point.
